newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia caps development allowance for 96/7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia caps development allowance for 96/7.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said he had directed the Development Allowance Authority to accept no further applications for a tax break on infrastructure borrowings.
"The Development Allowance Authority has advised me that (it) is currently assessing applications for total infrastructure borrowings of A$26.5 billion," Costello said in a statement.
This was seven times the value of applications actually approved since March 5 1995, when applications were invited, he said.
No further applications would be accepted until the next fiscal year began on July 1.

"This is consistent with the government's announcement on June 24 1996 that it would continue to keep infrastructure borrowings under review to ensure the programme is meeting its objectives," he said.
A development allowance entitles a business to deduct 10 percent of the value of plant and equipment from its taxable income, in addition to any other entitlements.
Under the scheme, business can finance approved infrastructure projects with bonds that pay tax-free interest.
Costello said that the programme would cost the government a maximum of A$150 million in 1996/97.
